t:
The Act entitled “An Act to authorize the Commissioners of the District of Columbia to plan, construct, operate, and maintain a sanitary sewer to connect the Dulles International Airport with the District of Columbia system”, approved June 12, 1960, as amended, is further amended (1) by striking out in section 4 (D.C. Code, sec. 43–1623(a)) “$25;000,000” and inserting in lieu thereof “$35,500,000”, and (2) by adding at the end of section 2(b) (D.C. Code, sec. 43–1621 (b)) the following: “Lump-sum payments made by an agency or local authority pursuant to the provisions of this section, and as reimbursement to the United States of funds loaned in compliance with section 4 of this Act, need not be appropriated, and may be made by the agency or local authority to the Secretary of the Treasury.”. The second sentence of section 4(a) of such Act is amended by striking out “Any loan advanced” down through and including “from the receipts credited to said fund” and inserting in lieu thereof the following: “Any loan advanced under this section shall be credited to the Metropolitan Area Sanitary Sewage Works Fund, and—

“(1) 
in the case of any loan advanced under this section before July 1, 1971, 50 per centum of such loan shall be repaid to the Secretary of the Treasury, and


“(2) 
in the case of any loan advanced on or after July 1, 1971, 100 per centum of such loan shall be repaid to the Secretary of the Treasury,

from the receipts credited to such fund”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the reference to an "agency or local authority" brings an outside party into a federal process. That reference only concerns how reimbursement payments are made to the Treasury; it is a financial mechanic, not consultation on a federal decision. The rest of the section raises a loan authorization ceiling and sets loan repayment percentages, with no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: Lump-sum payments made by an agency or local authority pursuant to the provisions of this section, and as reimbursement to the United States of funds loaned in compliance with section 4 of this Act, need not be appropriated, and may be made by the agency or local authority to the Secretary of the Treasury.

opus.w: This section raises the authorized amount and sets how loans for the Dulles sewer are repaid to the Treasury. A local authority appears only as a party making repayments, not as someone the federal government consults before deciding something. Paying money back is a financial obligation, not participation, so the tempting 'outside party involved' reading fails.
opus.s: Lump-sum payments made by an agency or local authority pursuant to the provisions of this section, and as reimbursement to the United States of funds loaned in compliance with section 4 of this Act, need not be appropriated, and may be made by the agency or local authority to the Secretary of the Treasury.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The section says an "agency or local authority" makes lump-sum payments to the Secretary of the Treasury, which brings a non-federal party into contact with the federal government. That fails the DEFINITION. These payments only repay loans and reimburse costs. The local authority isn't consulted or given a say before any federal decision, and the section has no hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. The rest of the section just changes a dollar limit and how loans are repaid.
